entities.name: Masjid Al-Istiqamah
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Masjid Al-Istiqamah (مسجد الاستقامة, 'Mosque of Steadfastness/Uprightness') is a mosque in Singapore — serving the island's Malay Muslim community within MUIS's (Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura) regulatory framework. The name 'Al-Istiqamah' (Arabic: الاستقامة) refers to the Islamic concept of steadfastness, uprightness, and remaining firmly on the straight path (sirat al-mustaqim), a core Quranic value invoked in the Fatiha prayer recited seventeen times daily in five prayers.

Singapore's mosque naming conventions frequently employ Arabic names reflecting core Islamic theological and ethical concepts — creating a landscape of religious institutions whose names collectively represent a theology of virtue: Al-Furqan (criterion), Al-Ghufran (forgiveness), Al-Huda (guidance), Al-Istiqamah (steadfastness) — together constituting a distributed theological curriculum in the urban landscape. This practice of meaningful naming is characteristic of Islamic religious architecture globally, where mosque names carry theological significance rather than merely locational or biographical reference.

The mosque serves its residential community through Friday prayers (khutbah, the sermon that provides weekly guidance to the congregation), daily prayers, Ramadan tarawih prayers, Eid celebrations, Islamic education classes, and social welfare services. Singapore's mosque network collectively manages the comprehensive religious life of approximately 600,000 Malay Muslims in one of the world's most efficiently governed city-states.
